scope: Control Systems Engineering: plan approximately 12–15 distinct, grounded patterns spanning feedback, stability, measurement, disturbances, actuator limits, identification and timescales. This invocation plans the collection only; a separate three-pattern pilot will test article production.
audience: Curious technical readers, software engineers and makers; explain engineering vocabulary and avoid pretending an educational example is safe controller design.
collection_goal: 12–15 carefully curated patterns with two reusable educational simulations, rather than a separate application for each article.

candidate_seeds.title: Close the Loop
candidate_seeds.insight: Measure actual outcomes and use feedback to correct deviations.

candidate_seeds.title: Tune for Stability Before Speed
candidate_seeds.insight: Faster responses can come at the cost of oscillation or instability, depending on plant, delay and controller.

candidate_seeds.title: Add Hysteresis
candidate_seeds.insight: Prevent repeated switching around a threshold.

candidate_seeds.title: Anticipate the Disturbance
candidate_seeds.insight: Use feedforward when upcoming disturbances can be measured or predicted.

candidate_seeds.title: Respect Actuator Limits
candidate_seeds.insight: Account for physical limits and saturation of the control mechanism.

candidate_seeds.title: Filter the Measurement
candidate_seeds.insight: Reduce noise while accounting for added phase lag and response delay.

candidate_seeds.title: Identify the System First
candidate_seeds.insight: Observe system dynamics before choosing a controller and parameters.

candidate_seeds.title: Separate Fast and Slow Loops
candidate_seeds.insight: Handle processes with different timescales while examining coupling.

notes: Treat the eight seeds as candidates requiring credible research and differentiation.
Thermostat: target 21 C, initial 18 C, outdoors 5 C; gain, thermal inertia, sensor delay, relay hysteresis, actuator limit, optional feedforward and window disturbance are adjustable.
Signals: deterministic noisy step, sample interval and low-pass time constant; show raw truth, sampled measurements and filtered measurements with quantitative error/lag observations.
Use source-supported physics and explicit model equations; do not claim high proportional gain alone always causes overshoot in a first-order delay-free plant.
Shared simulations are local educational assets staged through the existing patternverse-widget format. Never publish automatically.
